digest.component_or_area: blocking-link resolver in the hierarchy dependency graph
propositions: The blocking-link resolver decides comparability from the ticket type tier instead of position in the parent hierarchy, so it can record a different edge than requested and let a ticket block its own subtree.
Comparability must be structural (nearest common ancestor), so any two tickets sharing a parent may hold a dependency and re-typing a ticket must not silently rewrite the dependency graph.
No blocking edge may exist between a ticket and its own ancestor or descendant by any path into the resolver, enforced by recomputing redundancy from the resolved pair.
Cross-subtree blocking links must still auto-escalate and emit the machine-readable redirect record, keeping the escalation contract unchanged for callers.
Blocking edges already written under the old type-tier rule must be detectable store-wide and repairable in a single pass, shipped as a check within rebar doctor.
Self-blocking edges distort ready, next-batch and the parent-first claim cascade, handing parallel agents a wrong work order.
